title: Robust Hypothesis Testing with α-Divergence
access_routes_attempted: DOI/IEEE record; arXiv author manuscript linked to the published DOI
equivalent_verified_evidence: P0041 is a related later paper but is not needed to verify this record.
evidence_location: arXiv v3: Section II-A equations (1)-(7) defines dominated alpha-divergence balls and errors; Section II-B equations (8)-(10) establishes the saddle formulation; Theorem III.1 and equations (15)-(20) give the unique least-favourable densities and robust rule; Section III-C derives maximum robustness; Figure 10 and Section V state nonexistence beyond overlap boundary and limitations.
verified_result: For two dominated composite hypotheses defined by alpha-divergence balls, gives an exact saddle-value minimax Bayes test, least-favourable distributions and a computable robust likelihood-ratio rule. It also derives parameter regions where the least-favourable laws overlap and no minimax robust test of the specified form exists.
observation_regime: a fixed finite observation vector treated through its joint dominated law
upper_bound_or_construction: Theorem III.1: unique least-favourable densities and randomized robust likelihood-ratio rule from two nonlinear equations
lower_bound_or_converse: Exact overlap/robustness-radius obstruction in Section III-C and Figure 10; not a sample-complexity converse
gap01_effect: Establishes exact fixed-sample minimax testing for an important convex surrogate class, rejecting any broad claim that composite-versus-composite finite-sample minimax tests do not exist. It does not compute a test over the exact nonconvex EMU image families or optimize experimental design.
gap03_effect: Establishes an identifiability/overlap obstruction for divergence balls, weakening a broad impossibility-gap claim; it does not give replicate-count or design-specific EMU converses.
notes: Theorem requires dominated laws and convex alpha-divergence balls. The paper's stated open problem is monotonicity of threshold parameters with robustness radius or alpha.
